spots.name: Nuremberg Castle
spots.summary: Nuremberg Castle is a group of medieval fortified buildings on a sandstone ridge dominating the historical center of Nuremberg in Bavaria, Germany.

spots.name: Nazi Party rally grounds
spots.summary: The Nazi party rally grounds collectively describe a complex of megastructures and clearings which together occupy around 11 square kilometres (1,100 ha) of land to the southeast of Nuremberg, Germany. Six Nazi party rallies were held there between 1933 and 1938.

spots.name: St. Sebaldus
spots.summary: St. Sebaldus Church is a medieval church in Nuremberg, Germany. Along with Frauenkirche and St. Lorenz, it is one of the most important churches of the city, and also one of the oldest. It is located at the Albrecht-Dürer-Platz, in front of the old city hall.

spots.name: St. Lawrence
spots.summary: St. Lorenz is a medieval church of the former free imperial city of Nuremberg in southern Germany. It is dedicated to Saint Lawrence. The church was badly damaged during the Second World War and later restored. It is one of the most prominent churches of the Evangelical Lutheran Church in Bavaria.

spots.name: Frauenkirche

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Frauenkirche is a church in Nuremberg, Germany. It stands on the eastern side of the main market. An example of brick Gothic architecture, it was built on the initiative of Charles IV, Holy Roman Emperor between 1352 and 1362. The church contains many sculptures, some of them heavily restored.

spots.name: Germanisches Nationalmuseum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Germanisches Nationalmuseum is a museum in Nuremberg, Germany. Founded in 1852, it houses a large collection of items relating to German culture and art extending from prehistoric times through to the present day. The museum is Germany's largest museum of cultural history.

photo.author: The original uploader was Keichwa at German Wikipedia.

spots.name: Nürnberg Hauptbahnhof
spots.summary: Nürnberg Hauptbahnhof is the main railway station serving the city of Nuremberg in Germany. It is the largest station in Franconia and belongs to the 20 stations in the highest category of importance allocated by DB Station&Service.

names.ja: ニュルンベルク中央駅

spots.name: Schöner Brunnen
spots.summary: Schöner Brunnen is a 14th-century fountain located on Nuremberg's main market next to the town hall and is considered one of the main attractions of the city's Historical Mile. The fountain is approximately 19 metres high and has the shape of a Gothic spire.

spots.name: Ludwig Canal
spots.summary: The Ludwig Canal, is an abandoned canal in Southern Germany.

names.ja: ルートヴィヒ＝ドナウ＝マイン運河

spots.name: Palace of Justice

hours.note: Closed Tue

spots.summary: The Nuremberg Palace of Justice is a building complex in Nuremberg, Bavaria, Germany. It was constructed from 1909 to 1916 and houses the appellate court (Oberlandesgericht), the regional court (Landgericht), the local court (Amtsgericht) and the public prosecutor's office (Staatsanwaltschaft).

names.ja: ニュルンベルク刑務所

spots.name: Albrecht Dürer's House

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Albrecht Dürer's House is a Nuremberg Fachwerkhaus that was the home of German Renaissance artist Albrecht Dürer from 1509 to his death in 1528. The House lies in the extreme north-west of Nuremberg's Altstadt, near the Kaiserburg section of the Nuremberg Castle and the Tiergärtnertor of Nuremberg's city walls.

names.zh: 阿爾布雷希特·杜勒之家

spots.name: Fleisch Bridge
spots.summary: The Fleisch Bridge or Pegnitz Bridge (Pegnitzbrücke) is a late Renaissance bridge in Nuremberg, Germany. The bridge crosses the river Pegnitz in the center of the old town, linking the districts St. Sebald and St. Lorenz along the axis of the main market.

names.ja: 中央広場 （アドルフ・ヒトラー広場）

spots.name: Nuremberg Transport Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: The Nuremberg Transport Museum in Nuremberg, Germany, consists of Deutsche Bahn's DB Museum and the Museum of Communications. It also has two satellite museums at Koblenz-Lützel and Halle.

names.ja: ニュルンベルク交通博物館

spots.name: Heilig-Geist-Spital
spots.summary: The Heilig-Geist-Spital in Nuremberg was the largest hospital in the former Free Imperial City of Nuremberg. It was used as a hospital and nursing home.

spots.name: Documentation Center Nazi Party Rally Grounds
spots.summary: The Documentation Center Nazi Party Rallying Grounds is a museum in Nuremberg. It is in the north wing of the unfinished remains of the Congress Hall of the former Nazi party rallies.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Documentation Center Nazi Party Rally Grounds

names.ja: 党大会会場・記録センター

spots.name: City walls of Nuremberg
spots.summary: The city walls are the medieval defensive mechanism surrounding the old city of Nuremberg, Germany. Construction started in the 12th century and ended officially in the 16th century. They measured 5 kilometers around the old town.

spots.name: Grand Synagogue of Nuremberg

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Grand Synagogue of Nuremberg was a former Reform Jewish congregation and synagogue, located in Nuremberg, in the state of Bavaria, Germany.

spots.name: Nassauer Haus

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Nassauer Haus or Schlüsselfeldersche Stiftungshaus in Nuremberg is a medieval residential tower made of so-called red castle sandstone. Although originally built in Romanesque style, after several reconstructions the house is still characterized by Gothic style elements.

spots.name: Neues Museum Nürnberg

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Neues Museum Nürnberg (NMN) is a museum for modern and contemporary art and design in Nuremberg.

spots.name: Katharinenkirche, Nuremberg

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Katharina in Nuremberg, Bavaria, was an important medieval church, destroyed during the Second World War and preserved as a ruin.

spots.name: Nuremberg Zoo
spots.summary: Nuremberg Zoo is a zoo located in the Nuremberg Reichswald, southeast of Nuremberg, Germany. With an area of 67 hectares, approximately 300 animal species are kept by the zoo.

names.ja: ニュルンベルク動物園

spots.name: Historischer Kunstbunker

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Historische Kunstbunker is a tunnel complex under Nuremberg Castle in the old city of Nuremberg, southern Germany. It forms part of the Nuremberg Historic Mile.

spots.name: Johannisfriedhof (Nürnberg)
spots.summary: 14th-century graveyard with many famous citizens, including Albrecht Dürer and Adam Kraft. In summer the gardens are a riot of roses and other colourful flowers. You can walk here along Johannisstraße but the street is mostly modern, busy and uninteresting. Alternatively follow the river walk west from Hallertor. This eventually leads into Lindengasse which curls north to the church. Continue the

spots.name: Tiergärtnertor
spots.summary: Part of the labyrinth of tunnels underneath the city, but separate from the Felsengänge tour (listed above). During World War II this and other bunkers were converted into safe storage for the city's art treasures, with temperature and humidity controls and extra security. Frequent tours in German, but tours can be organised for up to 25 in English, French, Italian, Spanish and Czech.

spots.name: St. Martha

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Martha is a medieval church in the old town of Nuremberg in southern Germany. It is dedicated to Saint Martha. Since 1800 it has been a Reformed church, the community of which forms part of the Evangelical Reformed Church.

spots.name: Stadtmuseum Fembohaus

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: A merchant's house built about 1600, in late Renaissance style. Exhibition about the history of the city.

spots.name: Nuremberg City Hall
spots.summary: Nuremberg City Hall is located in the old town of Nuremberg, Germany, just east of the choir of the Sebalduskirche. It is part of the Historic Mile of Nuremberg as one of the city's sights. The imposing Renaissance building was designed by architect Jakob Wolff the Younger (1571–1620).

spots.name: Chain Bridge
spots.summary: The Chain Bridge is a pedestrian chain bridge in Nuremberg, Germany. The bridge crosses the river Pegnitz just a few meters upriver of Fronveste and Schlayerturm, fortifications in the course of the medieval city wall guarding the river's exit from the town.

spots.name: Pellerhaus
spots.summary: The Pellerhaus monument is an archive and library building on Egidienplatz in Nuremberg's old city centre. It extends over the area of the historic Pellerhaus and the historic Imhoff house to the east of it, which was rebuilt after the war in the contemporary design of the late 1950s.

spots.name: Nuremberg Toy Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Nuremberg Toy Museum in Nuremberg, Bavaria, is a municipal museum, which was founded in 1971. It is considered to be one of the most well known toy museums in the world, depicting the cultural history of toys from antiquity to the present.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

names.ja: ヴァイサー・トゥルム

spots.name: Staatstheater Nürnberg
spots.summary: The Staatstheater Nürnberg is a German theatre company in Nuremberg, Bavaria. The theatre is one of four Bavarian state theatres and shows operas, plays, ballets and concerts.

names.ja: ニュルンベルク州立歌劇場

spots.name: Burggrafenburg

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The central and oldest part. It was the permanent seat of the Burgraves (House of Hohenzollern) until it was destroyed in 1420. Today, you can see the Pentagonal Tower and the Walburgis Chapel. Their other residence, Cadolzburg (25 km west), is part of the combi-ticket.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: St. Egidien

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Egidien on Egidienplatz is the former Benedictine Abbey of Saint Giles (Egidienskirche), now a church in the former free imperial city of Nuremberg, southern Germany. It is considered a significant contribution to the baroque church architecture of Middle Franconia.

spots.name: Way of Human Rights
spots.summary: The Way of Human Rights is a monumental outdoor sculpture in Nuremberg, Germany. It was opened on 24 October 1993. It is sited on the street between the new and old buildings of the Germanisches Nationalmuseum, connecting Kornmarkt street and the medieval city wall.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site
Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: St. Elizabeth

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Elizabeth's is a Roman Catholic church in Nuremberg in southern Germany. It is dedicated to Elizabeth of Hungary.

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.name: St. Rochus Cemetery
spots.summary: St. Rochus Cemetery (Rochusfriedhof) is a cemetery in Nuremberg, Germany. It is located in the Gostenhof quarter.

spots.name: Nuremberg Exhibition Centre
spots.summary: The Exhibition Centre is relatively new. It offers over 160,000 m² of display area in twelve halls grouped around the central park.

spots.name: Historic tram depot (Historisches-Straßenbahndepot)

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sun

spots.summary: Trams since they began here in 1881. Several are in working order and when the museum is open, they make a leisurely grinding circuit of the city's public tramways.

spots.name: Gelbes Haus

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This is a mid-sized bar with two rooms, one with wood coated walls (which are nevertheless not "too heavy) and another one with the actual bar in it and in the style of the building; they serve a huge variety of classical, well-prepared cocktails and a good collection of spirits.

spots.name: Bratwursthäusle

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Restaurant in the old city centre specializing in roasted sausages. You can see many tourists there as it's one of the most frequented places to have a "Bratwurst" (grilled sausage). One of the most common packages is "Drei im Weckla" (three [sausages] in a bread roll).

spots.name: MUZclub

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A live music-oriented club with a nice garden for warm summer evenings which is operated by the non-profit music supporting association "Musikzentrale Nürnberg e.V." which regularly hosts concerts ranging from local scene festivals to somewhat more well-known groups.

spots.name: Albrecht-Dürer-Stube

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: A very traditional Franconian restaurant, frequented by locals and tourists alike. It is a good choice if you want to have some hearty local food in an unpretentious atmosphere. As the venue is small and popular, it is often necessary to have an advance reservation.

spots.name: Historische Bratwurstküche - Zum Guldenen Stern

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Restaurant in an old timber-framed house specializing in roasted sausages. Oldest sausage restaurant in the world, since 1419. Located in a small pedestrian zone in the Lorenz district, near Jacobsplatz, walkable distance (ca. 10 minutes) from the central station

spots.name: Club Stereo

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A small, nice club with changing offers (music genre highly depending on what the current event is), regularly offering nice concerts, too. The club is located in the basement and shares its entrance with the bar Vorraum, which is located on the ground floor.

spots.name: Restaurant und Biergarten Kopernikus im Krakauer Haus
spots.summary: A restaurant with a special beer garden which is nicely located on the city wall and also has tables along the city wall on a wooden path used with the fortification; the building housing the restaurant is a cultural centre connecting the region with Poland.

spots.name: Palais Schaumburg
spots.summary: One of the smaller beer gardens, this place exists for over 20 years now, nearly becoming an institution. It is especially popular amonsgst the somewhat more alternative and with vegetarians as it offers extensive choice for them.

spots.name: Mata Hari Bar

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: One of the places where it's easiest to get into conversations when you're coming by yourself. A small but atmosphere-packed place, where you can often hardly move but have great evenings talking about everyone and his brother.

spots.name: Hannemann

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A bar in between your grandma's style of living room (and similarly relaxed) and a hip modern place – if you want to chat with friends or just hang around easy-going people, that's one of the places you can choose.

spots.name: Kuhmuhne

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: If you want tasty burgers without going to a chain of restaurants and regional quality ingredients, this nice burger place is for you. Portions are quite Franconian (i.e. a little too big, maybe ;-)

spots.name: Suppdiwupp

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Great soups and hotpots served with fresh traditional style bread; the offerings change and there are not many dishes, but usually everybody should find something along her/his taste on the menu.

spots.name: Café Kirsch

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A cosy and inclusive café where people with and without handicaps cooperate. Unfortunately, at the site, access for people with disabilities is limited (elevated ground floor without a ramp).

spots.name: Eddy Would Attack

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A crazy combination of a bike repair shop and café, located centrally in Nurembergs red light area; offers breakfast, cakes etc. – and newspapers and bike journals to read

spots.name: Wurstdurst

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Serving the typical German currywurst. Ambiance and food top notch. Cozy atmosphere and super friendly staff. Also offering a tasty vegan currywurst.

spots.name: Wanderer and Bieramt

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Not a beer garden, but a place popular amongst locals and tourists. You can sit at the square, which becomes quite crowded on warm summer nights.

spots.name: Padelle d'Italia
spots.summary: A place to go for authentic Italian cuisine. It may be quite crowded and somewhat loud, but you will most probably find Italians here, too.

spots.name: Bra Kebap

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Good fresh ingredients. The dough for Dürüm is freshly prepared. You can choose between veal and chicken when it comes to meat.

spots.name: Brezen Kolb

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Brezen Kolb is the undisputed local hero in the Nuremberg pretzel business. Especially recommended with butter and chives.

spots.name: Würzhaus

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Franconian lunch, on evenings a rather upscale à la carte offering (as of groups of 8, a special menu can be prepared)
